content.title: Historical evidence for the resurrection
content.setting: College of the Holy Cross · 28 March 2006
content.description: Compare arguments about the resurrection with objections about what historical methods can establish.

claim.text: Craig argues that the resurrection best explains evidence about Jesus’ death and its aftermath. Ehrman challenges parts of that evidence and whether historical inquiry can establish a miracle.

content.hinge: Is the disagreement about what happened, how probable an explanation is, or what historians can conclude?
prompts: List the historical claims each speaker accepts and disputes.
Separate the probability of a miracle from the probability of the reported evidence.
Check whether an alternative is defended as true or offered as a possibility.
